verdicts.corrected_rule: argparse's HelpFormatter width = (COLUMNS if it parses as an int > 0 else terminal width of sys.__stdout__ else 80) - 2, and it wraps BOTH the usage line and the -h help body (option-help column + max_help_position), but NEVER the `{prog}: error: {message}` line. Exact boundary for prog 'test20_executable' (usage line = 71 chars): COLUMNS>=73 -> one line; COLUMNS<=72 -> wrapped with a 25-space continuation indent (= len('usage: ')+len(prog)+1); COLUMNS<=13 all collapse to the same one-token-per-line form with a 7-space indent (min text width clamps at 11) — COLUMNS=1,2,9,11,12,13 produced byte-identical output. Leading/trailing spaces and leading '+'/'0' are accepted by int() (' 40 ', '+40', '040' all wrap like 40). The error line stays on one line at every width: verified at COLUMNS=20 with a 152-char 'unrecognized arguments: ...' message, COLUMNS=5 with a 76-char invalid-int value, and COLUMNS=10 with a 76-char prog name. LINES has no effect. A reimpl that ignores COLUMNS matches only when stdout is not a TTY and COLUMNS is unset/invalid.

verdicts.rule: argv bytes are decoded as UTF-8 with surrogateescape; invalid UTF-8 in --a/--c passes the parser then crashes at .encode() with RC=1 + traceback; invalid UTF-8 in --f is reported by the parser with the lone surrogate rendered as \udcXX; locale (LC_ALL=C) does not change argv decoding.
verdicts.counterexample: NOT a refutation — I could not break it, and the locale claim is actually stronger than stated: LC_ALL=C, LC_ALL=POSIX, LC_ALL=C.utf8, LANG=C, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONUTF8=0+PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0, PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii and PYTHONIOENCODING=latin-1 ALL produced byte-identical stdout for `--a 'héllo' --c 'é'` (line 4 = b'\xc3\xa9', RC=0) and byte-identical stderr for `--f 'é'` (raw UTF-8 bytes 303 251 inside the quotes, NOT escaped), i.e. the frozen binary ignores PYTHON* io/locale env vars entirely. Fresh invalid-UTF-8 probes: --a $'\xff' -> RC=1, `File "test20.py", line 15` , `'\udcff' in position 0`; --a $'\xc3' (truncated) -> line 15, '\udcc3' position 0; --d $'\xfe' -> line 21, '\udcfe' position 0; --c $'A\xffB' -> line 17, position 1; --c $'AB\xff' -> line 17, position 2. Parser-side: --f $'\xff5' -> RC=2 `invalid int value: '\udcff5'` (od: literal backslash-u-d-c-f-f), --f $'5\xff' -> `'5\udcff'`, --g $'\xff' -> `argument --g: ... '\udcff'`, and LC_ALL=C gives identical bytes. Three additions a stderr-exact reimpl needs: (a) a MULTI-byte invalid run produces the plural form with no character shown — --a $'\xc0\x80' -> `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1: surrogates not allowed`, --a $'\xed\xa0\x80' -> `... position 0-2 ...`, and --f $'\xc0\x80' -> `invalid int value: '\udcc0\udc80'`; (b) --b/--e do NOT crash at .encode() but inside base58 — --b $'\xff' -> line 16 + `base58/__init__.py", line 118, in b58decode` + `line 30, in scrub_input` + `UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character '\udcff' in position 0: ordinal not in range(128)`, and plain non-ASCII (--b 'é') fails the same way with '\xe9'; (c) the `[PYI-NNNNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test20' due to unhandled exception!` trailer embeds the PID and is NOT reproducible (I observed PYI-88067, 88073, 88089, 88101, 88122, 88132, 88148, 88154 across runs vs their PYI-12659). Valid 4-byte UTF-8 (--a $'\xf0\x9f\x98\x80') is fine: RC=0, b'79jdou'.

verdicts.rule: There is no --version or any option other than -h/--help and --a..--g. Successful runs exit 0 with 12 stdout lines and empty stderr; help exits 0; all parse errors exit 2 with empty stdout.
verdicts.counterexample: Three independent counterexamples. (1) argparse's allow_abbrev makes prefixes of --help real, working options: `/workspace/dataset/test20_executable --h` -> RC=0 and the full 11-line help on stdout, empty stderr; same for `--he` and `--hel`. Short-option clustering also triggers help: `-hx` -> RC=0 + help, `-habc` -> RC=0 + help. A Node reimpl accepting only -h/--help would emit an error for all five. (2) 'help exits 0' is false when an explicit value is attached: `--help=x` -> RC=2, stderr `test20_executable: error: argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'`; identical for `--h=x` and `-h=x` (note `-hx` succeeds but `-h=x` fails). (3) 'help exits 0' is also false when an earlier token errors first, because -h only fires when reached: `--f abc -h` -> RC=2 `argument --f: invalid int value: 'abc'`, no help; whereas `-h --f abc`, `--zz -h` and `--a 1 -h --f abc` -> RC=0 + help. Bonus edge cases on 'successful runs exit 0 with 12 stdout lines and empty stderr': `... >/dev/full` -> RC=0 but stdout empty and stderr carries `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` + `Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>`; `... >&-` -> RC=0 with stderr `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flush'` (traceback file is `"<string>", line 1`). And there is a fourth outcome besides 0/2: `--f -1 --a 1 --b 2 --c 3 --d 4 --e 5 --g 2` never terminates (timeout 5 -> RC=124, zero bytes on both streams) because b58encode_int loops forever on negatives.
verdicts.corrected_rule: Accepted option spellings are --a..--g (exact, single-letter, so not abbreviable — `--ff 1` and `-a 1` are rejected) plus the help action reachable as -h, --h, --he, --hel, --help, or any -h<chars> cluster (-hx, -habc); matching is case-sensitive (--HELP, --He, --hx are NOT help). No --version/-V and no fromfile (@file) support. Both `--x V` and `--x=V` forms work, later duplicates win (`--a 1 --a 9` uses '9'), and empty values are legal (`--a '' ...` -> line 1 is b''). Outcomes: (a) RC=0 with exactly 12 stdout lines and empty stderr for a normal successful run — always exactly 12 even when values contain newlines/tabs, since print() emits bytes reprs (--c $'a\nb\tc' -> line 4 = b'a\nb\tc'); (b) RC=0 with 11 lines of help on stdout and empty stderr when a help spelling is reached before any error and has no '=' attached; (c) RC=2 with EMPTY stdout and exactly `usage: ...` + `{prog}: error: {msg}` on stderr for every parse error (verified ~20 ways: missing args, invalid int, `--a --b` -> 'expected one argument', 'ignored explicit argument', unrecognized args, positional/`--` leftovers); (d) RC=1 with a traceback for post-parse crashes; (e) non-termination for negative --f/--g. Ordering detail behind their --version evidence: unknown tokens are reported as `unrecognized arguments: ...` ONLY if all seven required options were supplied; otherwise the `the following arguments are required: ...` error wins and the unknown token is never mentioned (`--hx`, `-V`-first, `@somefile`, `-a 1 --b 2 ...` all produced the 'required' error).

verdicts.rule: Whitespace stripped by int() includes ' ', '\t', '\n', '\r', '\v', '\f' and Unicode spaces such as U+00A0 (NBSP).
verdicts.counterexample:
The listed 7 chars all confirmed (I tested each LEADING-only and TRAILING-only separately, plus all mixed on both sides: `--f $' \t\n\r\v\f\xc2\xa07\xc2\xa0\f\v\r\n\t '` -> RC=0, L6=7). But the phrase 'Unicode spaces' is dangerously over-general in BOTH directions:
(a) NOT all Python-isspace() chars are stripped. `--f $'\x1c7'` -> RC=2 `argument --f: invalid int value: '\x1c7'`; likewise $'\x1d7', $'\x1e7', $'\x1f7' all RC=2 -- even though CPython's `'\x1c'.isspace()` is True. (Reason: ASCII bytes pass through _PyUnicode_TransformDecimalAndSpaceToASCII unchanged and PyLong_FromString then uses C-locale isspace, which excludes 0x1c-0x1f.)
(b) NOT all 'space-like' Unicode chars are stripped: `--f $'\xef\xbb\xbf7'` (U+FEFF) -> RC=2 `invalid int value: '﻿7'`; U+200B -> RC=2 `'​7'`; U+200C -> RC=2 `'‌7'`; U+2060 -> RC=2 `'⁠7'`; U+180E -> RC=2 `'᠎7'`. This is a direct trap for a Node port: JavaScript's /\s/ INCLUDES ﻿ (Python rejects it) and EXCLUDES  (Python accepts it).
verdicts.corrected_rule: int() strips leading AND trailing runs of exactly this set, and nothing else: U+0009, U+000A, U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A (all 11 verified individually), U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000. Verified NOT stripped (RC=2): U+001C, U+001D, U+001E, U+001F, U+180E, U+200B, U+200C, U+2060, U+FEFF. Stripping happens before sign parsing, so `--f ' +7 '` -> 7 (RC=0) and `--f ' -7'` -> -7 (which then hangs in b58encode_int, RC=124 under timeout), but whitespace BETWEEN sign and digits is rejected: `--f ' - 7'` -> RC=2 `invalid int value: ' - 7'`, `--f '- 7'` -> RC=2. Whitespace-only is rejected: `--f ' '` -> RC=2 `' '`; `--f $'\xc2\xa0'` -> RC=2 `'\xa0'`; `--f $'\xe3\x80\x80'` -> RC=2 `'　'`. Internal whitespace rejected: `--f '7 7'` -> RC=2; `--f $'7\xc2\xa07'` -> RC=2 `'7\xa07'`. Do NOT implement this with JS /\s/ -- use an explicit codepoint set.

verdicts.rule: Non-ASCII Unicode decimal digits (category Nd) ARE accepted and converted by numeric value: Arabic-Indic, fullwidth, Thai, Mathematical Monospace all work. Non-Nd numerics (vulgar fractions, superscripts) are rejected.
verdicts.counterexample: No counterexample found across 17 Nd and 13 non-Nd probes. Accepted (RC=0, correct numeric value on line 6): U+0665 ٥ ->5, U+0660 ->0, U+06F5 ->5, U+096B ->5, U+09EB ->5, U+0E57 ๗ ->7, U+0F25 ->5, U+19D5 ->5, U+1C45 ->5, U+A8D5 ->5, U+ABF5 ->5, U+FF15 ->5, U+FF11FF12FF13 ->123, and ASTRAL-plane Nd (their evidence for these was invalid -- bash did not expand $'\U0001d7dd', the binary received the literal text `\U0001D7DD` and returned RC=2 `invalid int value: '\\U0001D7DD'`; I re-ran with explicit UTF-8 bytes): U+1D7CE ->0, U+1D7DD ->5, U+1D7F6 ->0, U+1D7FB ->5, U+104A5 ->5, U+1E959 ->9. Rejected (RC=2): No -> ½ ² ¹ ⁰ ₅ ⑤ ፲(U+1372) ↉(U+2189) ༫(U+0F2B) 𐩄(U+10A44); Nl -> 〇(U+3007) Ⅰ(U+2160) Ⅷ(U+2167); Lo -> 七.
verdicts.corrected_rule: Confirmed as stated, with these additions worth encoding: (1) astral-plane Nd works too (U+1D7CE/1D7DD/1D7F6/1D7FB/104A5/1E959 all accepted) -- note their 'Mathematical Monospace' label was on U+1D7DD which is actually DOUBLE-STRUCK FIVE; monospace five is U+1D7FB, also accepted. (2) Scripts may be freely MIXED: `--f $'1٢'` -> 12, `--f $'١2'` -> 12, `--f $'๗３9'` -> 739. (3) Underscore separators work between non-ASCII digits: `--f $'١_٢'` -> 12. (4) ASCII '+' works with them: `--f $'+٥'` -> 5. (5) Only the DIGITS are transliterated -- non-ASCII SIGN characters are rejected: U+FF0B `'＋7'` RC=2, U+FF0D `'－7'` RC=2, U+2212 `'−7'` RC=2. So implement as: map each codepoint through Unicode decimal-digit value, leave '+'/'-'/'_' as ASCII-only.

verdicts.rule: There is a hard limit of 4300 DIGIT characters. 4300 digits parse fine; 4301+ give `invalid int value: '<entire unmodified string>'` (not truncated). Underscores do not count toward the 4300; leading zeros DO count.
verdicts.counterexample: No counterexample found. Boundary re-verified independently: 4298 nines RC=0 (outB=6813), 4299 RC=0 (6814), 4300 RC=0 (6816), 4301 RC=2 (errB=4435), 4302 RC=2 (4436). Leading zeros pinned exactly: '0'x4300 -> RC=0 (outB=79); '0'x4301 -> RC=2; '0'x4299+'1' (4300 digits) -> RC=0; '0'x4300+'1' (4301 digits) -> RC=2. Non-truncation proven byte-exactly: errB == 132 + len(repr) for every over-limit case, including 100000 nines -> errB=100134 (=132+2+100000).
verdicts.corrected_rule: Confirmed, plus these verified extensions: (1) Neither surrounding whitespace nor the sign counts toward 4300: `--f "$(printf '%1000s'|tr ' ' ' ')$(9x4300)"` (5300 chars) -> RC=0, while the same with 4301 nines -> RC=2 errB=5435 (=132+2+5301, i.e. the 1000 spaces ARE echoed in the repr); `--f '+'+9x4300` (4301 chars) -> RC=0; `--f '+'+9x4301` -> RC=2 errB=4436; `--f '-'+9x4301` -> RC=2 errB=4436 (argparse accepts the leading '-' as a value, not an option). (2) Non-ASCII Nd digits DO count: 4300 Arabic-Indic ٥ (8600 bytes) -> RC=0 outB=6816; 4301 -> RC=2 errB=8736 (=132+2+8602, repr echoes them as raw UTF-8). (3) Underscore rule re-verified: 4300 nines with '_' every 4 digits (5374 chars) -> RC=0; 4301 underscored (5376 chars) -> RC=2 errB=5510. (4) Identical limit on --g: `--g` 4300 nines -> RC=0 outB=2517, 4301 -> RC=2 errB=4435. (5) Caveat for a reimplementation: over-limit and plain syntax errors are INDISTINGUISHABLE from stdout/stderr -- `--f 9x4300+'_'` (trailing underscore, only 4300 digits) also gives RC=2 with the same `invalid int value` wording.

verdicts.rule: The repr in `invalid int value: {v!r}` follows Python repr() rules exactly: single quotes normally; double quotes if value contains a single quote but no double quote; if BOTH, single quotes with the single quote backslash-escaped; backslash -> '\\'; newline -> '\n'; non-ASCII printable characters emitted raw (UTF-8), not \u-escaped.
verdicts.counterexample: Every claim they made is true, but the escape list is incomplete in a way that WILL break a Node port, because Python repr has named escapes for only \n \r \t \\ and the active quote -- NOT for \v \f \a \b (which JS/JSON escapers do emit). Verified: `--f $'a\vb'` -> od shows `' a \ x 0 b b '` i.e. `'a\x0bb'`, NOT `'a\vb'`. `--f $'a\fb'` -> `'a\x0cb'`. `--f $'a\ab'` -> `'a\x07b'`. `--f $'a\bb'` -> `'a\x08b'`. Also unstated: `--f $'a\rb'` -> `'a\rb'` and `--f $'a\tb'` -> `'a\tb'` (these two ARE named).
verdicts.corrected_rule: Quote selection and the four cited escapes are confirmed exactly (fresh evidence: `a"'b` -> `'a"\'b'`; `a'b` -> `"a'b"`; `a"b` -> `'a"b'`; `'` alone -> `"'"`; `"` alone -> `'"'`; `'"'` -> `'\'"\''`; `"'"` -> `'"\'"'`; `a'\b` -> `"a'\\b"`; `a'b"c\d` -> `'a\'b"c\\d'`; `a\b` -> `'a\\b'`; `a\\b` -> `'a\\\\b'`; `''` -> `''`). The full escape table must be: named escapes ONLY for \n (0x0a), \r (0x0d), \t (0x09), \\ (0x5c), and the enclosing quote; every other C0 control plus 0x7f -> lowercase \xNN (verified \x01, \x07, \x08, \x0b, \x0c, \x1b, \x1c-\x1f, \x7f). For non-ASCII, the test is Python str.isprintable(), not 'non-ASCII': printable -> raw UTF-8 (verified 'h\303\251llo', 七, U+1F600 emoji, ½, α, and combining mark U+0300 which IS printable -> raw `'a\314\200b'`); non-printable (Cc/Cf/Cs/Co/Cn/Zl/Zp/Zs) -> escaped with lowercase hex, width chosen by codepoint: \xNN below U+0100 (U+00A0 -> \xa0, U+0085 -> \x85, U+00AD -> \xad), \uNNNN in the BMP (U+200B -> ​, U+2028 ->  , U+3000 -> 　, U+FEFF -> ﻿, unassigned U+0378 -> ͸), \UNNNNNNNN (8 hex digits) above the BMP (U+E0001 -> \U000e0001). Additionally undocumented by them: bytes in argv that are not valid UTF-8 are decoded with surrogateescape and render as lone surrogates -- `--f $'\377'` -> `'\udcff'`, `--f $'a\377b'` -> `'a\udcffb'`, `--f $'\200'` -> `'\udc80'`, `--f $'a\303'` -> `'a\udcc3'`.

For ARGUMENT-DRIVEN runs with a writable stdout, exit codes are exactly {0, 1, 2} plus a non-terminating case:
- exit 0: 12 lines on stdout, empty stderr; OR -h/--help (11 lines on stdout, empty stderr).
- exit 2: argparse failure. stderr = a `usage:` block (ONE line at width >= ~72, WRAPPED into several `       `-continued lines when COLUMNS is small) followed by `<prog>: error: <msg>`. `<prog>` is basename(argv[0]). The error message is normally one line, but `unrecognized arguments: <argv joined by spaces>` is inserted un-escaped, so embedded newlines add lines. No `[PYI-...]` line ever (grep count 0).
- exit 1: an uncaught exception from one of the 12 statements; stderr = traceback + `[PYI-<n>:ERROR] ...` line.
- NO TERMINATION (must be killed): reached only when b58encode_int is called with a negative value AND no earlier statement raised. Precedence follows source line order 15(a),16(b),17(c),19(f),21(d),22(e),23(g): the FIRST failing statement wins, so a negative --g is unreachable if --e is bad, and a negative --f is unreachable if --a/--b/--c are bad. Verified still looping at 45 s (RSS 20.8 MB -> 23.1 MB, 100% CPU), so effectively infinite.
Outside the argument space other codes occur (143 direct SIGTERM, 153 SIGXFSZ, and exit 0 with an unwritable stdout). A Node port only needs to match 0/1/2 + hang for argument-driven cases.
verdicts.counterexample:
THREE independent counterexamples.

(A) exit-2 stderr is NOT always two lines. The 'unrecognized arguments' message interpolates argv VERBATIM (no repr), so a newline in an unknown token splits the line:
$ /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a x --b 2 --c x --d y --e 3 --f 1 --g 2 --q $'1\n2'
RC=2, stderr = 3 lines (cat -A):
usage: test20_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D --e E --f F --g G$
test20_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: --q 1$
2$
Same with a positional `... $'pos1\npos2'` -> 3 lines. And the usage line WRAPS with terminal width:
$ COLUMNS=30 /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --f zz
RC=2, stderr = 5 lines:
usage: test20_executable$
       [-h] --a A --b B --c$
       C --d D --e E --f F$
       --g G$
test20_executable: error: argument --f: invalid int value: 'zz'$
(COLUMNS=20 with no args -> 6 lines.) Also `<prog>` = basename(argv[0]), not a constant: copying the binary to `zz-renamed` yields `usage: zz-renamed ...` / `zz-renamed: error: ...`; a symlink named link.bin yields `usage: link.bin ...`.

(B) Negative --f/--g does NOT always hang. It hangs only if no EARLIER statement raises (line order a=15, b=16, c=17, f=19, d=21, e=22, g=23). Fresh probes, each under `timeout 8`:
  --a T --b '0' --c x --d y --e 3 --f -5 --g 2    -> RC=1 (ValueError, test20.py line 16), stdout 0
  --a T --b '0' --c x --d y --e 3 --f 1  --g -1   -> RC=1
  --a x --b 2 --c x --d y --e '0' --f 1  --g -1   -> RC=1 (ValueError at line 22, before line 23)
  --a x --b 2 --c x --d $'\xff' --e 3 --f 1 --g -1-> RC=1 (UnicodeEncodeError at line 21)
  --a $'\xff' --b 2 --c x --d y --e 3 --f -1 --g 2-> RC=1 (line 15)
  --a x --b 2 --c $'\xff' --d y --e 3 --f -1 --g 2-> RC=1 (line 17)
but --a x --b 2 --c x --d y --e '0' --f -1 --g 2  -> RC=124 (hangs; f at 19 precedes e at 22)

(C) exit 0 does NOT imply '12-line success'. With stdout unwritable the program exits 0 having printed NOTHING and emits a traceback with a third filename and no PYI line:
$ /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a T --b 2 --c x --d y --e 3 --f 1 --g 2 >/dev/full 2>/tmp/e; echo $?
0     (reproduced 3/3)
Traceback (most recent call last):$
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>$
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device$
Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>$
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device$
`>&-` -> RC=0 with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flush'`. `| true` -> RC=0 with a BrokenPipeError traceback.

(D) Other codes exist: direct `kill -TERM` during the hang -> RC=143 (6/6 trials, stderr 0 bytes); `ulimit -f 1` with a 27390-byte payload -> RC=153 (SIGXFSZ), stdout 0 bytes. The 124 they report is `timeout`'s own code, not the program's.
verdicts.rule: [1] There are exactly FOUR exit-code classes. (1) exit 0 = full 12-line success, or -h/--help. (2) exit 2 = any argparse failure: stderr is exactly two lines, `usage: <prog> [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D --e E --f F --g G\n<prog>: error: <msg>\n`, and NO `[PYI-...]` line. (3) exit 1 = any uncaught Python exception from the 12 computation statements: stderr is a traceback followed by a `[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] ...` line. (4) NO EXIT AT ALL (infinite loop, must be killed) when --f or --g is negative. A Node port MUST match exit codes 0/1/2 exactly; stderr text only loosely (see PID rule).

verdicts.counterexample:
I could not break this. Fresh probes, every one with stdout captured to a private `mktemp -d` file and measured with `wc -c`, all gave 0 bytes:
- exit 1: --b '0'; --b 'e-acute'; --e '0'; --b $'2\n0'; --a/--c/--d = $'\xff'; --b 'l'/'I'/'O'; --b $'\t2'; --b '2 2'; --e $'\xff'; and every negative-int + earlier-exception combo (O2, O4, O5, O6).
- exit 2: no args; --f zz; `--a` with no value; `--f=`; --f $'1\n2'; --q $'1\n2'; trailing `--`; stray `extra` positional; --f 1.5 / 1e3 / True; --f with 5000 digits; each single missing required arg.
- hang: --f -1 and --g -1 killed by timeout, direct SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGKILL -> stdout 0 bytes every time.
- pty via `script -qec "... 2>/dev/null"`: exit-2 log and exit-1 log contained only script's own header/footer, i.e. 0 program bytes on the tty.
- hostile stdout: `>/dev/full` -> 0 bytes; `>&-` -> 0 bytes; `ulimit -f 1`/`-f 2`/`-f 10`/`-f 20` with a 27390-byte payload -> RC=153 and 0 bytes in the output file (the kernel refuses the whole oversized write, so not even a partial flush lands).
The mechanism claim also checks out against /workspace/dataset/test20.py: lines 15-26 are all computation, lines 27-38 are all prints, so no partial-output interleaving is reachable from the arguments.
One boundary worth recording that does NOT contradict the rule: output can be truncated by a downstream reader on a SUCCESS run -- `prog --a <20000 A's> ... | head -c 8192` gave the reader 8192 bytes while the program exited 0 with empty stderr (the 64 KiB pipe buffer absorbed all 27390 bytes). That is truncated success, not a failure class with partial stdout.
verdicts.rule: [2] NO output ever appears on stdout in ANY failure class (all 12 prints happen after all computation). Verified stdout_bytes=0 for: surrogate in --a/--c/--d, invalid base58 in --b/--e, non-ASCII in --b/--e, negative --f, negative --g, non-int --f, missing --a, unknown --q. Also true when stdout is a TTY, a pipe, or a file.

verdicts.corrected_rule:
For exit-1 failures the traceback is:
  line 1: `Traceback (most recent call last):`
  then, per frame: `  File "<relpath>", line <N>, in <name>` (exactly 2 leading spaces), OPTIONALLY followed by `    <source line>` (4 leading spaces) and OPTIONALLY a caret/anchor line (11 leading spaces in the cases observed) -- these two extra lines appear IF AND ONLY IF the relative path resolves to a readable file from the process CWD.
  then `<ExcType>: <message>` (single line for every exception I could trigger)
  then `[PYI-<n>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test20' due to unhandled exception!`
All lines end with a single \n, no \r (od-verified). Frame filenames observed: `test20.py` and `base58/__init__.py` for the 12 statements, plus `<string>` on the interpreter-shutdown stdout-flush path (those runs exit 0). No absolute paths and no site-packages prefix -- that part is confirmed.   So 100 KB takes 15.5 s and the largest --c= payload is exactly 131067 bytes (arg '--c=' + payload = 131071 = MAX_ARG_STRLEN-1; confirmed independently with /bin/echo: argbytes=131071 rc=0, argbytes=131072 rc=126). Past that the program never executes.

(b) line4bytes = payload_len + 4 FAILS on a payload of pure printable ASCII with no conventional escapes, because Python's bytes repr backslash-escapes ' when the payload also contains ":
  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a T --b 2 --c="a'b\"c" --d y --e 3 --f 1 --g 2
    rc=0 plen=5 line4=<b'a\'b"c'> line4bytes=10   (rule predicts 9)
  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a T --b 2 --c="'\"" ...
    rc=0 plen=2 line4=<b'\'"'> line4bytes=7    (rule predicts 6)
  Contrast: --c="it's" -> b"it's" line4bytes=8 = plen+4 (delimiter flips to ", no escape); --c='a"b' -> b'a"b' = plen+4.

(c) Not all --c values are valid payloads at all. Invalid UTF-8 in argv survives as a lone surrogate and .encode() raises:
  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a T --b 2 --c=$'\xff' --d y --e 3 --f 1 --g 2
    rc=1 stdout_bytes=0
    File "test20.py", line 17, in <module>
    UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\udcff' in position 0: surrogates not allowed
  Same rc=1 for $'\xc3', $'\xe9', $'\xed\xa0\x80', $'\xf5\x80\x80\x80'. Valid multibyte is fine: '€' (plen 3, b58len 10), '😀' and $'\xf4\x8f\xbf\xbf' (plen 4, b58len 11). Note stdout is entirely EMPTY on failure -- all 12 prints are suppressed because every computation precedes the first print.

(d) Bonus: rc=0 does not imply empty stderr. The N=131067 run above emitted, with rc=0:
    [PYI-230398:WARNING] Failed to remove temporary directory: /tmp/_MEIjfhITZ
  Intermittent -- 0/25 occurrences on the small baseline; leftover /tmp/_MEI* dirs are present on the box.
verdicts.corrected_rule: Payloads succeed with rc=0 and byte-exact output up to the OS argv ceiling: max --c payload is 131067 bytes using the --c=VALUE form (131068 -> rc=126 'Argument list too long', program not executed). Runtime is quadratic in payload length, not flat: 10 KB ~300 ms, 40 KB ~2.7 s, 100 KB ~15.6 s, 131 KB ~27.7 s -- budget harness timeouts accordingly. --c values that are not valid UTF-8 (lone surrogates from argv surrogateescape) exit rc=1 with UnicodeEncodeError at source line 17 and an EMPTY stdout (no partial lines). Line 4 is repr(payload) + newline; its byte count is payload_len + 4 only when every payload byte renders as itself, i.e. all bytes in 0x20..0x7e, no backslash, and NOT both ' and " present (when both are present the ' becomes \' costing +1 each). Bytes outside 0x20..0x7e render as \xNN / \t / \n / \r. Finally, rc=0 does not guarantee empty stderr: the PyInstaller bootloader intermittently prints '[PYI-...:WARNING] Failed to remove temporary directory: /tmp/_MEI...' on an otherwise successful run.

verdicts.rule: [3] Reproduction caveats: argparse rejects a --c value beginning with '-' (rc=2) -- use --c=VALUE. $(printf '\n') strips trailing newlines, so a newline-only payload must be embedded non-trailing (e.g. $'a\nb'). Any nested command inside a while read loop must redirect stdin (</dev/null) or use read -u 3, otherwise nested processes silently consume loop lines.
verdicts.counterexample:
All three sub-claims are over-general.

(a) argparse does NOT reject every '-'-leading value in space form. Command:
  t(){ /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a T --b 2 "$@" --d y --e 3 --f 1 --g 2 >/tmp/av_o 2>/tmp/av_e; echo "rc=$? line4=$(sed -n 4p /tmp/av_o)"; }
  t --c '-abc'  -> rc=2  error: argument --c: expected one argument
  t --c '-5'    -> rc=0  line3=b'PWjDGkgy'    line4=b'-5'     ACCEPTED
  t --c '-42'   -> rc=0  line3=b'2iMckjazVX'  line4=b'-42'    ACCEPTED
  t --c '-3.5'  -> rc=0  line3=b'8ZVm9JxZRs3' line4=b'-3.5'   ACCEPTED
  t --c '-a b'  -> rc=0  line3=b'8bEkN525hvc' line4=b'-a b'   ACCEPTED (contains a space)
  t --c '-'     -> rc=0  line3=b'6Bv6P73'     line4=b'-'      ACCEPTED (lone dash)
  t --c '--'    -> rc=2 ; t --c '---x' -> rc=2 ; t --c '-h' -> rc=2 ; t --c '-e' -> rc=2 (note: -h does NOT print help, it is the same 'expected one argument' error)
  This is argparse's _negative_number_matcher / space heuristic, not a blanket dash rule. --c=VALUE works for all of them (--c=-abc -> rc=0 line4=b'-abc').

(b) A newline-ONLY payload is perfectly passable; only command substitution is the problem:
  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a T --b 2 --c=$'\n' --d y --e 3 --f 1 --g 2
    rc=0 line3=b'2CSMBfn' line4=b'\n'   == node b58encode_check(Buffer.from([10])) = 2CSMBfn
  (Separately confirmed the shell fact: v=$(printf '\n'); ${#v} == 0; v2=$(printf 'a\n\n\n'); ${#v2} == 1.)
  So the 'must be embedded non-trailing' instruction is unnecessary -- use $'\n' with the --c= form.

(c) The stdin-stealing hazard applies ONLY to nested commands that actually read stdin. With /tmp/av_lines.txt = L1..L4:
  while read -r x; do echo "saw:$x"; wc -l >/dev/null; done < /tmp/av_lines.txt        -> prints only saw:L1   (hazard real)
  while read -r x; do echo "saw:$x"; /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a T --b 2 --c "$x" --d y --e 3 --f 1 --g 2 >/dev/null 2>&1; done < /tmp/av_lines.txt -> prints saw:L1 saw:L2 saw:L3 saw:L4  (NO hazard)
  while read -r x; do echo "saw:$x"; node -e "1" >/dev/null 2>&1; done < ...            -> all 4 lines  (NO hazard)
  while read -r x; do echo "saw:$x"; node /tmp/av_noop.js >/dev/null 2>&1; done < ...    -> all 4 lines  (NO hazard)
  while read -r x; do echo "saw:$x"; cat /tmp/av_lines.txt >/dev/null; done < ...        -> all 4 lines  (NO hazard)
  And the executable ignores stdin entirely: printf 'JUNK\n' | ...exe... -> rc=0, line3=b'EYVuQ4z' (identical to no-stdin run).
  Therefore neither the executable nor node could have caused their 'phantom mismatches' in cases 14/15; that diagnosis is unsupported (actual cause: not established by me either).
verdicts.corrected_rule: Harness hygiene: (1) In space form (--c VALUE), argparse rejects a '-'-leading value with rc=2 'argument --c: expected one argument' ONLY when it is not a lone '-', not a bare negative number matching ^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$, and contains no space; '-5', '-42', '-3.5', '-a b' and '-' are all accepted. Just always use --c=VALUE and the distinction stops mattering. (2) Pass control characters with ANSI-C quoting on the --c=VALUE form -- --c=$'\n' yields a newline-only payload just fine (rc=0, line3=b'2CSMBfn'). Avoid $(printf ...) for any value with trailing newlines, since command substitution strips them. NUL is unrepresentable in argv at all (--c=$'a\x00b' arrives as b'a'). (3) Only nested commands that READ stdin (wc, head without a file, sort, etc.) steal while-read loop lines; test20_executable, node -e, node script.js, and cat FILE do not. Redirecting </dev/null is still cheap insurance, but a mismatch cannot be blamed on this unless a stdin-reading command is in the loop.
